newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse plans lower transaction fees in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse plans lower transaction fees in 1997.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange is likely to cut its transaction fees for brokers to 0.1 percent from the present 0.14 percent of a transaction value, a bourse deputy president said on Wednesday.

"It has always been our aim to lower the fees and we're trying to make it happen this year, initially from 0.14 percent to 0.12 percent and later towards the end of the year to 0.10 percent," Ryszard Czerniawski told Reuters.
Waldemar Wolinski, deputy head of Kredyt Bank SA brokerage, said the move could help brokerages improve their profits if they decided to keep commissions for clients unchanged.
"I don't think commissions (for clients) will be lowered because commissions for clients are already at a low level," Wolinski said.

Polish brokerage houses grossed 36 million zlotys in 1995, down from a 140 million zloty gross in 1994 because of lower operating margins on stock market transactions, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said last April.
